note: One accepted error, and it is the single most valuable finding of the whole reverse pass: a false quantitative claim in the game's own narrative, of a kind no content read-through and no playtest would catch.

accepted.reason: REAL DEFECT OF THE ORIGINAL. index.html:769-772 prints three quarterly actuals against a predicted $41,730 and then claims 'Every quarter lands within ±2% of the model.' Q3's actual of $40,880 is 2.04% below the prediction of $41,729.72. The game tells a student that a model performed inside a tolerance it did not meet — in the case whose entire subject is judging whether a model is fit to budget on. Fix in a forward build: change the Q3 actual to $40,900 or above, or soften the prose to 'within about 2%'.
accepted.whyItMatters: This is the defect the adversarial review predicted the framework would wave through, on the grounds that narrative numbers could be declared exempt. They cannot: a declaration under narrativeNumbers carries an obligation, and a prose quantifier over declared numbers is itself evaluated. The distinction that makes it work is that 'within X' is a BOUND and must hold exactly, while 'off by X' is a stated measurement compared at its own precision.

fixedByRoundTrip.defect: Three of the eight step types are not data-driven at all. renderClassify (index.html:968) hardcodes its three cost lines, renderPickPoints (1037) hardcodes the selection rule, and renderResidual (1078) hardcodes its eight-point dataset, the OLS solve, the 1.35 tolerance factor and the bad-fit reference. The LEVELS entries for those steps are just {type, quip}.
fixedByRoundTrip.howTheSpecFixesIt: classify carries its buckets and items; select-from-set carries the dataset, the count and the rule; the residual sandbox becomes an extension whose params hold the points, the objective, the tolerance factor and the reference fit. An instructor can now change the numbers without touching a renderer.
fixedByRoundTrip.consequence: Roughly 60 authored strings and numbers move out of render functions and into addressable content fields — which is also what makes check N2 able to see them at all.

fixedByRoundTrip.defect: The mixed-cost total $2,800, the annual splits $9,600 / $21,600, the high-low spread 4,800/400, the prediction $6,600 and the unexplained 35% are all typed as literals in prose, with no link to the primitives they come from.
fixedByRoundTrip.howTheSpecFixesIt: Each becomes a named derivation over knowledge.params, and check N2 refuses any number in graded text that is not reachable from a param, a dataset or a derivation. Editing the water bill now propagates, or breaks the build.

expressiveRangeContributed: modes[]: solo vs class competition is not a local override — it changes the scoring formula, the hint labelling, turn rotation and projector typography, touching four agents' field sets at 13 sites. It forced a first-class cross-cutting construct that no other fixture needed.
A resource meter with a payout rule: client trust starts at 100, floors at 20, loses 5 per hint and 12 per wrong answer, and cashes out 1:1 into score at segment end in solo mode only.
The base-streak-speed scoring model, the only one in the corpus where the award depends on how the answer was reached rather than only on what it was.
narrativeNumbers with checked prose quantifiers — see the accepted finding above.
